config.motion: This house would tax sugary drinks

points: Price works where willpower fails, especially on heaviest-drinking households.
Levy shifts buying, funds school water and dental care, pushes reformulation.
Regressive effect is answered by pairing with subsidies on water and produce.
Labelling alone has not moved the dial; price reaches the autopilot shopper.
Imperfect category line still beats no line at all.
Sugary drinks category has no defensible edge; line drawn by lobbyists.
Levy is regressive; subsidy promise is a separate bill nobody has passed.
Harm already disclosed on label; price punishes careful and careless alike.
Information targets both; label better, measure honestly, leave grocery budget alone.
As written, levy taxes whatever drafting room decides; subsidy not in motion.

verdict.keyDisagreement: Whether a sugary drink tax as written can be justified given its regressive incidence and undefined category, or whether better labelling achieves the same without those costs.
verdict.rationale: The Opposition scored higher on Evidence, Rebuttal, Clarity and Persuasion, and its closing effectively pressed the Proposition on the undefined category and the out-of-motion subsidy. The Proposition was clear and conceded ground, but its case rested on an unpassed subsidy and an unmeasured behaviour change, leaving the Opposition's alternative stronger on the scores.
